newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods wants level playing field for pools.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods wants level playing field for pools.

text.p: Littlewoods Organisation, the privately-owned shops to leisure group, called on the British government to create a level playing field for its football pools business and the National Lottery.
Chairman James Ross said football pools turnover had continued to suffer severely from the impact of the lottery, and was down nearly 30 percent in the first half of this year.

"We'd still like the government to take some real action, like not make us pay more (tax) than the rate of VAT," he said in a telephone interview. Littlewoods' tax rate was 26.5 percent, while the Lottery pays 12 percent, he said.

Ross said the group was spending six million stg on advertising the re-launch and early indications were that the marketing campaign had doubled sales in the first few weeks. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
